RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the November 28, 2006/Agrahayana 7, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Promotion of tourism in Assam
†*81. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the details of schemes formulated
by Government for development and
promotion of tourism in Assam; and
(b) the details of amount allocated,
released and spent by the Central
Government for implementation of
proposals regarding tourism in the State
during  the last three years, project-wise?
Upgradation of Biju Patnaik Airport,
Bhubaneswar
*82. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to upgrade
Biju Patnaik Airport (Bhubaneswar) in
Orissa to the international standards;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the time-frame within which the
above project would be initiated and
completed; and
(d) whether during this upgradation scheme
a sizable number of temporary workers
working now shall be made permanent?
Development of Arka Khetra of Konark
*83. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
develop Arka Khetra of Konark to make it
more attractive for the tourists;
(b) whether this project would be
funded by the IOC;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) what is the status of development of
eco-tourism with central assistance in Orissa?
Loans to farmers at concessional
interest rates
†*84. SHRI MOTI LAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) when Government made an
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

27
announcement to provide loans to farmers
at concessional interest rate;
(b) the States where concessional loans
have been provided to the farmers so far
and the percentage of Co-operative Banks
therein;
(c) the arrangements made by
Government to ensure that the farmers do
not take loan from moneylenders;
(d) the arrangements made by
Government to provide loans immediately
to the farmers in the rest of the States also;
and
(e) the hurdles in providing loans to
farmers through Co-operative Banks and
by when, these would be removed?
Shortage of Commercial pilots
†*85. SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn towards the shortage of
commercial pilots in the country; and
(b) if so, the details of steps taken to
meet the shortage of commercial pilots in
the country?
Losses suffered by domestic airlines
*86. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost all
the domestic airlines are incurring low
profits and even in some cases losses as
compared to the previous year;
(b) if so, the details thereof; airline-
wise;
(c) what are the reasons for this; and
(d) the details of steps taken by
Government in this regard?
Training of pilots on CAT-III system
*87. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  have reviewed
the preparedness of different airlines to
deploy the required number of pilots
trained to navigate jets to thick foggy
conditions, during the fast approaching
winter season, with the help of CAT-III
Instrument Landing System (ILS);
(b) if so, the results thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that several airlines
fall significantly short of the required
number of pilots as per the laid down
norms;
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken to persuade the
concerned airlines to employ more trained
pilots or reschedule their flights during the
poor visibility conditions period ahead to
avoid inconvenience to passengers?
Protection of ASI monuments and
museums
*88. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRI AJAY MAROO:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ajanta,
which is among the first examples of early
Buddhists architecture  pertaining to 2nd
century BC, is now facing problem of seepage;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

28
(b) if so, what is the number of caves
which are under threat of water seepage;
(c) the details of  the steps taken or
proposed to be taken by Government to
protect this world heritage site;
(d) whether there is  requirement of
more security personnels for curbing the
illegal trafficking and the protection  of
various ASI's monuments and museums in
the country; and
(e) if so, what is Government's response
thereto?
Tourists safety from riots and bomb blasts
*89. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
drastic fall in the number of tourists visiting
Aurangabad and monuments in its vicinity
like Ajanta and Elora caves, a Taj-Mahal
Look-like Bibi-ka-Maqbara and recently
discovered 50,000 year old meteorite
impact Lonar Crater;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor  as local
traders and others connected with the
tourist industry are greatly suffering as they
do not have any alternative means of
livelihood; and
(c) whether it is due  to apprehensions
amongst prospective tourists regarding
their safety due to riot and recent bomb
blasts  in Gujarat, Mumbai, Srinagar; etc.
and how  the situation is going to be tackled?
Non-completion of irrigation projects
on time
*90. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether irrigation facility is available
only to 39 per cent of agricultural land out
of a total 14 crore hectare agricultural land;
(b) whether this situation has occurred
only due  to non-completion of irrigation
projects on time;
(c) the details of irrigation projects lying
pending together with the reasons for their
non-completion and the quantum of funds
incurred on these projects so far; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
provide irrigation facilities to each farmer?
Development of hotel infrastructure
to promote tourism  in Orissa
*91. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre is drawing up an
ambitious plan under which the seat of
'patta chitra' Raghurajpur and tourist's
paradise Daringbari are set to emerge the
next hotspots in Orissa under the rural
tourism project;
(b) if so, the details of the project; and
(c) what is the action plan of the Centre
to develop hotel infrastructure in the State
to promote tourism?
New standards for Navratna status to
PSUs
*92. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering new rules and standards for
according Navratna status to PSUs;

29
(b) if so, the details thereof and how
they differ from the existing ones;
(c) whether Navratna PSUs which do
not conform to the new rules will lose their
status; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Reduction in petroleum prices
*93. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are considering
reduction of petroleum prices in view of
decline in international prices of crude oil;
(b) if so, the road-map and time frame
thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Completion of projects with Iran
*94. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Iran has been
keeping India hanging on each and every
energy project like C.N.G. Project, L.N.G.
Project, Hydrocarbans Project for the last
several years;
(b) if so, what are the details of projects
which are still hanging fire at present and
since when; and
(c) by when these are likely to be
approved?
New norms for vehicle insurance
*95. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether new norms for vehicle
insurance are going to be adopted  from
next financial year which would not be based
only on purchase value of the vehicle;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the criteria on which the
new insurance policy will be based; and
(d) whether Government have fixed any
criteria or it will be left at the discretion of
individual insurance company which may
lead to arbitrariness?
Maintenance and rehabilitation of
water bodies
*96. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted any census on the water  bodies
in the country, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether it is a fact that over the
years the water bodies have decayed, if so,
what are the reasons for such a decay and
which are the regions where such a decay is
faster;
(c) which are the Centre, State and
District level organizations responsible for
the maintenance and rehabilitation of such
water bodies and whether any
responsibility has been fixed for the decay
in water bodies;
(d) whether Government have any plan
to revive these water bodies; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not
the reasons therefor?

30
Increase in prices of commodities
*97. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a  fact that inflation has
crossed 5 per cent in the month of October
this year and is continuously increasing;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether the prices of foodgrains,
pulses and vegetables have risen abnormally
during the last one year due to inaction on
the part of Government; and
(d) if so, the steps proposed to be taken
by Government to bring down the prices
and to decrease the inflation?
Indifferent  treatment to urban Co-
operative Banks
*98. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
RBI is giving step-motherly treatment  to
Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs);
(b) the reasons for not granting licences,
even to good UCBs to open new branches
in States which have signed MoU with
RBI;
(c) whether Government are aware that
RBI is giving same treatment to good and
weak UCBs which is adversely affecting
their performance and public image and is
weakening the cooperative movement; and
(d) if so, whether Government will
impress upon RBI to issue licences for new
branches to sound and strong UCBs in
those States which have already signed
MoU with them?
Investment of pension fund in stock
market
†*99. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to invest pension fund in the  share
market;
(b) whether employees unions are
supporting this move;
(c) whether Government have
formulated any plan to encounter the risk
factor arising out of investing pension fund
in the share market; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
International airport project at
Hyderabad
*100. SHRI  NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the progress made so
far  on international airport at Shamshabad
on the outskirts of Hyderabad;
(b) the time likely to be taken to
complete this project; and
(c) the details of the funds spent so far
on this project and the works completed
till date?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the November 28, 2006/Agrahayana 7, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance; Heavy Industries
and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
Commencement of flights by German
Airlines between Goa and Germany
554. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether German Airlines Condor has
commenced commercial flights between
Goa and Germany;
(b) if so, the frequency of these flights;
(c) whether these flights will be
restricted to the tourist season;
(d) the details of the conditions of
license under which the airlines will be
operating; and
(e) whether any other foreign airlines
have sought permission to operate to and
from Goa?
Reduction in ATF cost
555. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Aviation Turbine Fuel
(ATF) costs are 70 per cent higher in India
which work out to almost 40 per cent of
the total cost input of Indian carriers;
(b) whether Iindian airports will soon
have ATF outlets operated by global ATF
suppliers and if so, to what extent this will
help in reducing the ATF costs for Indian
carriers; and
(c) whether Bangalore, Hyderabad,
Delhi and Mumbai airports are considering
the open access model for the supply of
ATF and if so, how soon these facilities are
likely to be in place?
Casual labours in Indian Airlines
556. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of casual labours working
in Indian Airlines on 90 days basis at
various regions of Mumbai, Kolkata,
Chennai and Delhi (region-wise break up)
and for how long they have been working;
(b) whether these casual labours have
been empanelled for regular vacancies to be
filled up as per the Recruitment and
Promotion Rules of Indian Airlines; and

131
(c) whether the vacancies will be filled
up by the Indian Airlines before the
proposed merger of Air India and Indian
Airlines is completed?
Leasing of aircrafts
557. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) what is the fleet strength of Indian
Airlines and Air India as on 31st October,
2006 (type-wise, owned and leased break
up);
(b) the number of aircrafts which have
been flying out of the leased and owned
aircrafts and how many are grounded as on
31st October, 2006;
(c) the payment conditions for leased
aircrafts when these aircrafts are grounded;
(d) whether lease amount is payable
even if the aircraft is grounded; and
(e) if so, the terms and conditions of the
payment?
Open sky policy
558. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Directorate General of Civil
Aviation has moved a proposal to follow
an open sky policy for four months
beginning from November, 2006;
(b) if so, whether during the open sky
policy, international airlines are allowed to
increase frequency or bring in larger aircraft
irrespective of capacity that they are
allowed under the existing air services
bilateral agreement;
(c) if so, whether Government are keen
to ensure passengers do not feel
inconvenience and seats are easily available
during the upcoming winter season; and
(d) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Merger of Air India and Indian
Airlines
559. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to merge Air India and Indian
Airlines;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the details of benefits of this merger
for Government and all employees?
Theft at airports
†560. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether certain incidents of thefts
in the flights between Delhi-Mumbai,
Delhi-Kolkata and Mumbai-Kolkata have
come to notice;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the extent of loss incurred by each
passenger as a result of such thefts and the
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

132
compensation given by the airline to
make up for the loss; and
(d) the action taken by Government
in order to check such type of incidents
in future?
Discontinuance of route dispersal
guidelines
561. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that regional
airlines are being encouraged to improve
connectivity to small cities;
(b) if so, the details of the steps taken/
proposed to be taken in this regard;
(c) whether there is any plan to
discontinue Government's policy of route
dispersal;
(d) if so, the details thereof including
the arrangement to provide connectivity
to uneconomic routes; and
(e) the role envisaged for the National
carrier 'Indian' in the growing
regionalisation of aviation sector?
Growth rate of passengers
562. SHRI R. SHUNMUGA-
SUNDARAM: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the growth rate of air passengers,
air cargo and airlines operations in the
non-metro cities in Tamil Nadu; and
(b) what steps have been taken to gear-
up the airport authorities and the airlines
to meet the growth rate?
Purchase of aircrafts equipped with
CAT-III B System
563. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of airports in the country
which are equipped with CAT-II System
for assisting planes to land at fog hit
airports;
(b) whether pilots of Indian Airlines and
Air India have been trained to operate the
flights during foggy weather using CAT-II
system;
(c) whether it is a fact that most of the
Boeing airplanes in India including the ones
yet to be delivered are not compatible to
operate using the CAT-III B system, and
airline companies, in a bid to save costs,
have not opted for these system separately;
and
(d) if so, what action Government have
taken in this regard?
Decongestion of airports
564. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the growth of air traffic during the
last three years by percentage and the
number of aircrafts;
(b) the additional facilities provided
during the same period to handle the
increased air traffic;
(c) the reasons for regular delay in
landing and take-off of flights from major
airports in the country; and
(d) the steps taken to decongest
airports?

133
New greenfield airports
565. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the greenfield airports
currently under construction in the country
alongwith the estimated dates of beginning
of their operations; and
(b) the details of greenfield airport
projects currently in the process of
approval?
Upgradation of airports in
Rajasthan
566. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of airports in
Rajasthan have been identified for
upgradation and which would be of
international standard;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the road-map and timeframe
thereof?
Funds for aviation sector
567. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a total of
Rs. 26,000 crore would be required for the
indian aviation sector for purchase of
aircrafts replacement of old fleet and
modernization of airports, etc.;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether it is also a fact that effective
capacity of existing facilities can be
augmented through innovative and
inexpensive means?
National Aviation Board
568. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that one way to
achieve quick results in the civil aviation
sector is to have a National Aviation Board
with full financial and executive powers;
(b) if so, whether Government are
considering to set up a National Aviation
Board; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Operation of private airlines
†569. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the private airlines
operating in the country at present;
(b) whether it is a fact that most of
these airlines do not fulfil the conditions
and criteria fixed by Government at the
time of issuing licenses to them;
(c) whether it is also a fact that these
private airlines are neglecting them despite
of repeated warnings by Government;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
details of the action taken by Government;
and
(e) if not, the details of surprise
inspections carried out by Government in
this regard?
Development of new airports in the
country
†570. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
development of airports is not keeping pace
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

134
with the volume of increased air traffic in
the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
aeroplanes have to keep hovering
unnecessarily upto 20 minutes before
landing;
(c) if so, what is the plan of Government
to reduce the air traffic jam;
(d) the details of the efforts being made
to develop other airports of the country
apart from those located in metropolitan
cities, State-wise;
(e) whether Government are also
considering constructing of new airports;
and
(f) if so, the details thereof State-wise?
Development of Khajuraho airport
†571. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the land is
being acquired from the State Government
of Madhya Pradesh free of cost to develop
Khajuraho airport and what is the quantum
of land acquired so far;
(b) the status of development works
like enlargement of airstrip and other
construction work after acquisition of land;
and
(c) whether the work has been
completed, if not, by when the same is
likely to be completed?
Promotion of low cost airlines
572. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the market share of various airlines
according to Government record;
(b) whether it is a fact that low cost
airlines are ruling the aviation business;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government are taking any
steps to encourage these low cost airlines
by reducing taxes and providing
exemptions;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) whether this step will help common
man to fly?
Installation of CAT-III A landing
system
573. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Airlines and Air India
are incurring heavy losses every year due
to cancellation/delay of flights due to dense
fog or otherwise;
(b) if so, the estimated loss incurred by
Indian Airlines and Air India due to
cancellation/delay of flights during the last
two years;
(c) whether the CAT-III A system
installed at various airports to facilitate
landing in foggy conditions proved
ineffective;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) the amount spent on installation of
such system; and
(f) the corrective measures taken/
proposed to be taken by Government in
this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

135
Formation of federation of Indian
Airlines
574. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the full-service and low-
cost carriers of Indian aviation industry
have formed a Federation of Indian Airlines
(FIA);
(b) whether the Federation in its first
meeting, the pricing aspects of the industry
was reportedly discussed and if so, whether
this amounts to attempt on cartelisation
detrimental to the interests of air travellers;
and
(c) whether the Competition
Commission of India has raised concerns
over the formation of such a Federation
and if so, the details thereof?
Setting up of Aviation Grid
575. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to setup an Aviation Grid to ensure
infrastructure development in the country
in view of the boom in aviation industry;
(b) if so, the details of its constitution
and precise functions;
(c) the steps so far taken in this regard;
and
(d) the immediate plan in hand for the
grid?
Shortage of pilots with IA and AI
576. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P.
GOYAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the number of pilots who have left
Indian Airlines/Air India for the last three
years;
(b) whether it is a fact that Indian
Airlines/Air India are facing shortage of
pilots;
(c) if so, the reasons for not appointing
more pilots; and
(d) what steps are taken by Government
to solve this problem?
Recommendations of Paul Committee
on airtraffic management
577. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether he has been handed over a
list of far reaching measures by the Roy
Paul Committee on air traffic management
to tackle the worsening congestion of flights
over Delhi and Mumbai airports that include
getting the IAF station at Palam shifted to
Hindon and freeing the space for commercial
flights at Delhi;
(b) whether the former Civil Aviation
Secretary and member of Naresh Chandra
Committee has drawn up an action plan to
decongest the skies by at least 20-30 per
cent at both airports; and
(c) if so, how many recommendations
of the Committee has been implemented or
are under implementation?
Private airlines in international
services
578. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state the criteria of allowing
certain private airliners to operate
international flights?

136
Improvement of air services in
Sikkim
579. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether any special scheme has been
chalked out by Government to improve
the air service in the North Eastern Region
particularly in Sikkim;
(b) if so, the details thereof'; and
(c) the amount spent or likely to be
